Sign a payload as a JWS

Source: R/jws.R
jws_sign.Rd

jws_sign() signs payload with one key, or with several through jws_signer(), and returns the JWS in the compact, flattened JSON or general JSON serialization (RFC 7515).

Usage

jws_sign(
  payload,
  key,
  alg = NULL,
  header = NULL,
  unprotected = NULL,
  format = c("compact", "flattened", "general"),
  b64 = TRUE,
  detached = FALSE
)

Arguments

payload

The payload: a raw vector, or a single string taken as UTF-8 text.

key

A jwk, or a list of jws_signer() objects for several signatures.

alg

The signature algorithm, such as "HS256" or "RS256". NULL takes the key's own alg.

header

Further protected header members, as a named list.

unprotected

Unprotected header members, as a named list. Only the JSON serializations carry them.

format

"compact", "flattened" or "general". Several signatures need "general".

b64

Whether the payload is Base64url-encoded in the signing input and the token. FALSE follows RFC 7797.

detached

Whether to leave the payload out of the token. The verifier then supplies it to jws_verify().

Value

The JWS, as a single string.

Details

The protected header holds alg, the key's kid unless header or unprotected sets one, and the members of header. With b64 = FALSE, the payload is signed and carried unencoded (RFC 7797), and the header gains b64: false and crit: ["b64"].

A header's names must be unique and not empty at every depth, a member may appear in only one header, and values must be of a type JSON can represent. Anything else is a zujose_argument_error.

The algorithms are HS256, HS384 and HS512 with an oct key, and RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384 and PS512 with a private RSA key of at least 2048 bits, and ES256, ES384 and ES512 with a private EC key on P-256, P-384 and P-521 respectively. RS* signatures are deterministic; PS* and ES* ones are randomized. An ES* signature is r followed by s, each of fixed length, as RFC 7518 section 3.4 specifies.

Examples

key <- jwk_oct(as.raw(1:32), kid = "k1")
token <- jws_sign("hello", key, alg = "HS256")
token
#> [1] "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImsxIn0.aGVsbG8.X2gFwW_6UvgW7Bh1zZ_A-dSWyDix7IWMYIFm10uAmnw"
rawToChar(jws_verify(token, key, algorithms = "HS256")$payload)
#> [1] "hello"
